xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:DisclosureOfNotesOnComposition:
The Company convened meetings of statutory board level committees, namely Nomination & Remuneration Committee and Risk Management Committee, during quarter ended March 2025, fulfilling the statutory requirements of composition and quorum including for Independent Director. There was no Independent Director during 24.01.2025 to 27.03.2025.
The Company made appointment of three Independent Directors w.e.f. 28.03.2025. Re-constitution of statutory board level committees with nomination of Independent Directors were made on 08.04.2025.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:DisclosureOfNotesToAnnexure1Ex:
As on 31.03.2025, the Board comprised of 7 Functional Directors (including Chairman), 1 Government Nominee Director and 3 Independent Directors. Considering the compliance requirement of atleast 50% of Independent Directors of the Board Strength, there was a shortfall of five (5) Independent Directors. Accordingly, the MoPNG, Government of India, had been requested vide letter dated 27.01.2025 and 08.01.2025 to fill the shortfall of Independent Directors. ONGC is a Government Company and power of appointment of directors (including independent director) is vested with the Govt. of India (GoI).
The Company had requisite number of Independent Directors as on 31.03.2025 for reconstitution of Audit Committee, Nomination and Remuneration Committee, Stakeholder Relationship Committee and Risk Management Committee as per SEBI (LODR), Regulations, 2015. As 3 Independent Directors were appointed on 28.03.2025, the Company re-consituted the Committees on 08.04.2025. During this period, no abovementioned Committee meeting was convened.

xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:AnyOtherInformationForDisclosu:
It is informed that being a Government Company, power of appointment of Directors (including Independent Directors) is vested with the Govt. of India (Gol) in terms of provisions of Articles of Association (AoA) of the Company. The requirement for appointment of requisite number of Independent Directors were submitted to the Government of India (GoI) vide letters dated 08.01.2025 and 27.01.2025. The copy of said letters were also submitted to Stock Exchanges.
It may be noted that the said non-compliance with regard to the composition of the Board was not within the control of the Company and the Company has been regularly pursuing with the GoI for appointment of Independent Directors to meet the compliance requirements.
Considering the above position, both the exchanges have been requested to waive-off the above mentioned fine levied on the Company.

xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:CurrentStatusOfTheLitigationOr:
The Company had received demand orders from GST and Service Tax Department at various work centres on account of GST and Service Tax on Royalty in respect of Crude oil and Natural gas. Appeals against such orders have been filed before various Tribunals/ Courts.
A demand order has been issued by Rajasthan GST Department to ONGC for non-payment of GST on Royalty for Other JV partners i.e. Vedanta and CEHL share @ 35% respectively (PI in PSC) in unincorporated Joint Venture (UJV for Pre NELP block RJ-ON-90/1 for the period 01.04.2020 to 14.05.2020 (primary term of PSC was valid up to 14.05.2020). However, ONGC is paying GST under protest for its own share of PI in JV i.e. 30%. Writ has been filed against the demand order for the period 01.04.2020-14.05.2020 in Jodhpur High Court on 03.04.2025.
